instagram_reel.script:
Ever poured a Pinot Grigio and thought, why is this copper? That’s ramato. 

Ramato comes from the Italian word rame, which means copper. It’s Pinot Grigio made with skin contact, so the grape gives the wine that pink-gold colour. 

And this is not some weird new trend. It’s actually the traditional style of Pinot Grigio in Friuli, in northeast Italy. 

The cool part? Skin contact doesn’t just change the colour — it gives the wine more texture and a little more grip. So if you’ve only ever known pale, neutral Pinot Grigio, ramato is a really fun surprise. 

I broke down how it compares to rosé in the full post — go have a read.

tiktok.script:
Your Pinot Grigio might be copper on purpose. That style is called ramato. 

Ramato comes from rame, the Italian word for copper, and it’s Pinot Grigio made with extended skin contact. That’s what gives it the colour — not a trick, not an additive. 

And this is actually the traditional way Pinot Grigio was made in Friuli, in northeast Italy. So in a way, the pale version is the newer one. 

What I love is that ramato gives you more texture and a little more grip than the super light Pinot Grigio people usually expect. 

So if you’ve ever seen it in a glass and thought, what am I looking at? — now you know.

linkedin.post:
Ramato is a great example of how winemaking method shapes both style and perception.

If you’ve ever poured a Pinot Grigio and found a copper or pale pink hue instead of the pale straw colour most people expect, you’ve likely encountered ramato. The colour comes from extended skin contact, which also brings more texture and a little tannic grip.

What’s especially interesting is that this is not a novelty. Ramato is the traditional style of Pinot Grigio from Friuli-Venezia Giulia in northeast Italy, predating the modern stainless steel, quick-press approach that became standard in the mid-20th century.

For trade, it’s a useful reminder that consumer expectations around “white wine” are often shaped more by technology and market style than by grape identity alone.

For anyone educating drinkers, ramato is a very approachable entry point into skin contact wines: familiar grape, surprising result, and a clear story behind the glass.

quote_card: Rosé is a red grape made to taste light. Ramato is a white grape made to show more of what it’s actually capable of.
